findings.title: Early interpolation defeats the $__range split exclusion
findings.body: runSplitQuery now runs every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables before querySupportsSplitting. That helper replaces Grafana range macros ($__range, $__range_s, $__range_ms) from request.scopedVars using the full request range. querySupportsSplitting then calls isQueryWithRangeVariable on the already-rewritten expr, so the $__range token is gone and the query is treated as splittable. The comment on querySupportsSplitting says these queries must not be split because the macro is meant to be interpolated on the backend against each request's own time range. After this change each chunk is executed with the full-range duration baked in (for example count_over_time({app="x"}[7d]) on every 1-day slice), so merged results overlap or over-count and Loki load grows with the selected range. The new tests only cover $__auto and $step, and the default test templateSrv does not expand $__range, so this production path is untested. Interpolate only after classifying queries on the raw expr, and leave $__range* in the expression sent to the backend.

findings.title: Shard queries are template-interpolated twice, including ad-hoc filters
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery now maps every target through applyTemplateVariables(query, scopedVars, request.filters), then splitQueriesByStreamShard rewrites those expressions with interpolateShardingSelector and calls runSplitQuery. runSplitQuery unconditionally applies applyTemplateVariables again on that rewritten expr, with the same request.filters still set. applyTemplateVariables is not idempotent: ad-hoc filters are inserted into the stream selector on each call, so a sharded query gets duplicate matchers (or a failed/misplaced insertion once `| drop __stream_shard__` is already in the LogQL). A second template replace can also expand `$` sequences that appeared in variable values. The updated shard test expects applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times for a single target (once here plus once per split group) and only uses an idempotent replace mock, so it locks in the double application instead of catching duplicate filters. Interpolate once, before shard selector injection, and do not run applyTemplateVariables again inside runSplitQuery for targets that are already interpolated.
